newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS-Investors miffed by EVN results.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Investors miffed by EVN results.

text.p: Austria's regional utility EVN reported on Tuesday a record pre-tax profit for the 1995/96 year but investors were miffed, saying the group had let them down by delaying news of a flat net profit.

EVN Energie-Versorgung Niederoesterreich AG, said in a press release pre-tax profit in the year to August 31, 1996, jumped 24.4 percent to 1.484 billion schillings ($141.2 million) and that it would increase its dividend by two schillings to 25.

But only at its news conference later in the morning did EVN reveal that net profit for the year was flat at 667.4 million due to higher tax payments of 468.6 million from 180 million the previous year.

"This is ridiculous -- such a delay between the release of pre-tax and net profit," one irate London-based analyst said. "And how can they say they're increasing their dividend and then later announce a flat net profit? It was misleading."
The Vienna market reacted swiftly to the results, where EVN was hammered down 79 schillings to 1,469, before recovering a touch to stand 3.88 percent lower at 1,487 in an overall flat market.

Traders said they were disappointed with the earnings as EVN had long been flagging the news that it would turn in a spectacular set of results, yet the pre-tax figure was at the bottom end of analysts' forecasts and net profit was a clear disappointment.
"The market was obviously expecting more. The firm had flagged 1995/6 would be a very good year so the flat net profit was a bit of a surprise," said a trader.
EVN's record pre-tax profit of 1.484 billion schillings was below most analysts' expectations of around 1.5-1.7 billion.

"EVN had risen strongly recently in expectation of a good set of results. These figures have taken the wind out of its sails," another trader said. Over the past month EVN had added on 11 percent in a sputtering market.
The market was also disappointed with EVN's statement that it expected 1996/7 pre-tax profit to be below the 1.484 billion posted in 1995/6.
"We have budgeted for a slightly lower pre-tax profit in the coming year," chief executive Rudolf Gruber told a news conference.

"The temperature development in 1995/6 was a one-off. Despite economic growth in Lower Austria above the national average and expansion in gas and district heating, such a result is not repeatable given normal weather conditions."
He added that EVN aimed to maintain its basic 23 schillings divdend payment in 1996/7. For 1995/6 it announced 23 schillings plus a two schillings bonus.
